General budget support to the implementation of the poverty reduction strategy/Government Operational Plan together with 18 other GBS donors within the framework of a joint MoU signed in March 2009.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2013Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The overall objective of the intervention is to support the implementation of Mozambique's poverty reduction strategy (PARP), the overall objective of which is to reduce consumption poverty from 54.7 to 42% by 2015. A new household survey is expected to become available during 2015, so recent poverty figures are not yet available.
The results during 2013 were broadly in line with those of previous years. The continued expansion of services in education, health water & sanitation and social protection has a positive effect on poor people’s life, although the quality of services remain a problem and sometimes even increases as the systems expand. Underlying problems include slow institutional reform, weak public financial management and problems with logistics. Despite continued strong economic growth during 2013, there are no convincing signs that growth is becoming inclusive, i.e. poor people do not participate or benefit from the economic growth to the extent that that would be expected. The growth in sector of small scale farmers (70-80% of the population) remained below average, whilst job creation is slow (acknowledging that statistics are unreliable). The GoM delivered reasonably well on the results it had committed to achieve in this area, but it is generally recognized the set target do not adequately reflect progress on inclusive growth. Better policies to improve agriculture productivity and create jobs, especially in small and medium sized enterprises are needed.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
